# Welcome {.unnumbered}

This book is the public tutorial for the `fdid` R package, which implements
Factorial Difference-in-Differences (FDID) for panel data settings where all
units experience a common event and differ in a baseline factor `G`
[@xu2026factorial].

The tutorial is organized around the target the analyst wants to report. The
binary and discrete-`G` workflow comes first. Continuous-`G` workflows then
separate scalar slopes, level curves, derivative curves, observed-population
average derivatives, fixed-reference contrasts, and support diagnostics.

Main user-facing functions:

- `fdid_prepare()` reshapes long panel data into the wide format used by
  `fdid()`.
- `fdid()` estimates binary, discrete, kernel continuous-`G`, and DML
  continuous-`G` FDID models.
- `fdid_contrast()` reports continuous-`G` level contrasts from stored curve
  objects.
- `fdid_derivative()` reports fixed-`G` derivative values from stored curve
  objects.
- `summary()` and `plot()` display fitted objects.

## Organization

- [Chapter @sec-start] covers installation, loading, and the required data
  shape.
- [Chapter @sec-binary] covers the original binary/discrete-`G` workflow.
- [Chapter @sec-continuous-overview] maps user targets to continuous-`G`
  methods, support checks, and reporting views.
- [Chapter @sec-kernel-continuous] covers kernel level and derivative curves.
- [Chapter @sec-dml-continuous] covers DML scalar, flexible-curve, and
  incremental targets.
- [Chapter @sec-visualization] documents current base-graphics plotting.
- [Chapter @sec-reporting-inference] centralizes summaries, contrasts,
  derivatives, and interval labels.
- [Chapter @sec-sensitivity] gives applied sensitivity checks.

Please report bugs on [GitHub](https://github.com/xuyiqing/fdid/issues) with
minimal replicable code, data, and a treatment-status plot when relevant.
